question: Refer to the exhibit. Which two Cisco UCS components are upgraded as a result of the configuration? (Choose two.)
context: Exhibit: UCS Manager 'Install Infrastructure Firmware' wizard, step 2 'Install Infrastructure Firmware'. Fields shown: Firmware Installer: Ready, Name: default, Description: Infrastructure Pack, Infra Pack: 3.2(3d)A, Service Pack: <not set>, Force checked, Evacuate unchecked, Infrastructure Upgrade Schedule: Admin State Untriggered, Owner Local, Max Number Of Concurrent Tasks Unlimited, Upgrade Now checked.
imageNote: Screenshot of the Cisco UCS Manager 'Install Infrastructure Firmware' wizard (step 2), showing Infra Pack version 3.2(3d)A being applied with 'Upgrade Now' checked.
explanation: Not revealed in the source material (solution not expanded). The Infrastructure Firmware Pack in Cisco UCS Manager typically upgrades UCS Manager itself, the Fabric Interconnects, and the I/O Modules (IOMs) — the answer is provisional pending verification.
theory: Installing an Infrastructure Firmware pack through Auto Install upgrades the components that make up the UCS domain's control and data-plane infrastructure — the fabric interconnects, Cisco UCS Manager, and the I/O Modules (IOMs) — as a single, all-or-nothing operation. Server-facing components such as BIOS, board controller, and adapter firmware are not part of the Infrastructure pack; they are upgraded separately in the Install Server Firmware stage via host firmware packages. Recognizing that IOMs and UCS Manager (not adapters/BIOS) sit inside the infrastructure bundle is the key distinction here. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Firmware Upgrades, Auto Install)
